refnamediv.refpurpose: Realtime scheduling policy and watchdog service

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-rtwatchd is a system service that changes the scheduling policy of threads of unprivileged processes to realtime scheduling (SCHED_RR or SCHED_FIFO) or to a negative nice level on request. It is intended as a safe mechanism to make realtime scheduling available to unprivileged applications, such as audio servers, without granting them RLIMIT_RTPRIO. It implements the D-Bus API of RealtimeKit, and is a drop-in replacement for it.
The service enforces the following policies when handing out realtime scheduling:

listitem.para: Only clients which have set RLIMIT_RTTIME to a value no larger than the one configured with --rttime-max= are granted realtime scheduling.

Realtime scheduling and high priority are always handed out with SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK set, so that the scheduling parameters do not leak into child processes. This ensures realtime fork bombs cannot be used to circumvent RLIMIT_RTTIME.
The number of users, processes per user and threads per user that may be supervised at the same time is limited, as is the number of requests per user per time window.

refsect1.para: In addition, the service runs a canary based watchdog: its main loop regularly signals a watchdog thread that runs at a very high realtime priority. If the main loop does not get any CPU time for a while (which suggests that realtime threads are starving the system), the watchdog demotes all realtime threads the service handed out back to SCHED_OTHER, and refuses further requests for a while.
The service also integrates with systemd-logind.service8: before the system is suspended all realtime and high priority threads are demoted, and they are promoted again after the system resumed.

The service is activated on demand and runs as the unprivileged systemd-rtwatch user, with only the CAP_SYS_NICE and CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH capabilities. When it exits it demotes all threads it promoted.

refsect1.title: D-Bus API
refsect1.para: The service implements the org.freedesktop.RealtimeKit1 D-Bus interface, compatible with the one implemented by RealtimeKit, under the bus name of the same name. See org.freedesktop.RealtimeKit15 for details.

refsect1.title: Varlink API
refsect1.para: The service also implements the io.systemd.RTWatch Varlink interface, on the /run/systemd/io.systemd.RTWatch socket. It provides functionality equivalent to the D-Bus API: MakeThreadRealtime() and MakeThreadHighPriority() take an optional thread (a ThreadId object, defaulting to the main thread of the calling process), and the requested priority or nice level. A ThreadId object consists of the process the thread belongs to (a ProcessId object, defaulting to the calling process), the kernel thread ID (defaulting to the main thread), and optionally the inode number of the thread's pidfd (on kernels that support thread pidfds), which, if specified, is used to verify that the thread ID has not been recycled. ResetKnown(), ResetAll(), Suspend() and Resume() correspond to the D-Bus methods of the same names. Describe() returns the enforced policy and current state. List(), which must be called with the more flag, enumerates the threads currently made realtime or high priority, one reply per thread, including the unit and command line of the process and the name of the thread. Unprivileged clients only see their own threads. Watch(), which must be called with the more flag, reports events as they happen: threads being made realtime or high priority (with the same thread information as List() returns), threads being demoted or promoted again (via the calls above, or because the system goes to sleep or wakes up), and the canary based watchdog taking action. Use varlinkctl introspect /run/systemd/io.systemd.RTWatch io.systemd.RTWatch to see the full interface definition.

The same polkit actions as for the D-Bus API are used for MakeThreadRealtime(), MakeThreadHighPriority(), ResetKnown(), ResetAll(), Suspend() and Resume(). Watch() is authorized via io.systemd.rtwatch.watch, since its events include information about the processes of all users. By default both require administrator authentication; root is always allowed.

refsect1.title: Options
refsect1.para: The following options are understood. Most of them correspond to settings in rtwatchd.conf5, and take precedence over them. In order to change them, override ExecStart= of systemd-rtwatchd.service with a drop-in file, though using the configuration file is generally preferable.

listitem.para: Overrides SchedulingPolicy= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides OurRealtimePriority= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides OurNiceLevel= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides MaxRealtimePriority= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides MinNiceLevel= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides RTTimeMax= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Override UsersMax=, ProcessesPerUserMax=, and ThreadsPerUserMax= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Override ActionsBurstSec= and ActionsPerBurstMax= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides Canary= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Override CanaryCheepSec= and CanaryWatchdogSec= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Overrides CanaryRefuseSec= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Override CanaryDemoteRoot= and CanaryDemoteUnknown= in rtwatchd.conf5, see there for details.
Write D-Bus introspection data of the specified object path to standard output, and exit.
